page: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8223CL processor with 36 physical cores and 72 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and delivering a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score placing in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with cached small-block reads reaching 3707.05 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 208.99 GB/sec. However, single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core metrics, falls into the average category. Notably, LLM text generation speeds are weak, with the 7B model generating only 6.95 tokens per second, though prompt processing speeds remain average.

The c5.18xlarge offers high compute density and strong multi-core throughput, making it a cost-efficient option for parallel processing workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The lack of bundled local storage means all disk I/O must traverse the network, which may introduce latency for storage-heavy operations. This instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads such as batch processing, distributed analytics, high-performance web serving, and database operations, as demonstrated by its strong performance in Redis SET operations and PassMark database benchmarks.
